items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: My brother-in-law, I don’t think you’ve met him, Ryan Shaw is his name. He’s a real good trumpet player from the west coast. A few years ago I was at his house

ctx.x: I just want to say this. I heard a professor one time, and he said, “Oh, yeah, Louis Armstrong. The guy would sometimes play a whole solo with one note.” Oh yeah? And I mean it’s horrible to hear something like that because this is a guy that’s teaching young people hopefully to play jazz. And if you don’t teach someone to respect and investigate Louis Armstrong, I don’t think you’re teaching them the right thing. Because he was a force to be reckoned with, to say the very least.

My brother-in-law, I don’t think you’ve met him, Ryan Shaw is his name. He’s a real good trumpet player from the west coast. A few years ago I was at his house and he had this, well it was a textbook and it was a real dry textbook. I can’t remember the exact title, but it was something like Principles of Brass Playing in the Modern Orchestra. And it was talking about symphonic brass playing. And I said, “what should I see about this,” because it looked pretty boring, a big textbook. He said, “well look up, I…

Not enough can be said about Louis Armstrong, let’s face it. My daughter has a little friend in New Orleans and the little friend’s babysitter, once I went to pick them up to take them for a cool drink or something. And the lady gets in the car and she says, “you’re a jazz musician, right?” I say, “yeah.” She says, “you know my cousin played trumpet.” I say, “really, who is it?” She says, “Louis Armstrong.” Armstrong, man, I got the shakes man.
